reviewer: Claude agent review (Opus), not a human historian
text: 2026-10-11: approved on a third read of story.json (introduction, twelve scenes with paragraphs, alt texts, facts and dramatised lists, summary, ನಿಮಗೆ ಗೊತ್ತೇ?, visitToday, provenance, disclosure, content note) and facts.json, after the first pass returned nine text blockers and three image blockers and the second pass two small blockers, all now fixed.

Blockers found on the first pass and fixed: (1) source commentary inside scenes ('the stone does not say' in scene-09 and scene-11, 'the stones call him' in scene-02, 'his stones tell' in scene-03), now told as events or as the scribe's choice; (2) 'among sand dunes' at Talakad (scene-04 prose and alt), against the bible; (3) 'three words' for the two-word ಹೋರಾಡಿ ತೆಗೆದುಕೊ; (4) Damodara made a third man beside Adiyama and Dama, now one man with the choice disclosed; (5) 'after 1126 he stopped bearing another's title', contradicted by No. 384 (c. 1135) and EC V's Chalukya acknowledgments to 1174, now 'raised his sword north again', with summary line 7 to match; (6) Machikabbe's words rendered as a question, now 'it has fallen to me to remain' in the prose, facts.json and story.facts; (7) a scene-11 sentence in which the king 'lost' himself; (8) undisclosed inferences (Dorasamudra as the place of the 1121 council, the father's death on the same hill, the son born 'the same day'), now dropped or softened to 'at that time'; (9) the seven hells credited to Belgola records of 1118–1120, now to Bl 124 (1133) in scene-03's dramatised list and in f-gangaraja-titles. Second pass: scene-12's dramatised list had added a line giving 1141 to Sastri (now 'the subtitle's 1142 is Derrett's year'), and scene-04's alt still put the Chola camp across the river after the picture was regenerated.

Every name, number, year, relationship and quotation was compared with hoysala-verified.md: Malepar-ol-ganda, Tribhuvanamalla, Ereyanga and Dhara, 'manda Poysala'; the Sala legend and its hare and chamara variants (told as ಐತಿಹ್ಯ); the three princes, the Santara Jagaddeva and the necklace ornament; the pedigree of Gangaraja, the purna-kumbha, drohagharatta and the seven hells; Talakad as Rajarajapura and Talaikkadu; 'Fight and take it'; Dama's back, the ascetic's disguise and the dog's food; Kete-Nayaka's shield as earthquake or thunder and his entry behind the king; the Kaveri corpses, the wells, the south wind and Yama's moustache; Talakadu-gonda, Vira-Ganga and the coins; Kirtinarayana with four villages and a tank; Kannegal (twelve samantas, 'Let go!', mounted, 'as if a sport', stores and vehicles); 'delighted, delighted; ask', Parama and Govindavadi, Subhachandra's feet; the enclosure, the line under Chavundaraya's, Jinanathapura, 'hundred-fold' and 'stand erect'; Belur 1117 (Chaitra bright fifth, 'called Chenna', 'Obeisance to Kesava and Siva', the grantees, Shantala's titles and her Siva temple); Savatigandhavarana, Santi-Jina, Prabhachandra, Brihaspati and Vachaspati; 1131, Saka 1053, Monday, Sivaganga; Machikabbe's month's fast before three gurus; Bokimayya and the engraver; 1133, Boppa, Drohagharatta-Jinalaya, Bankapura, the king's words, Vijaya-Parsva and Vijaya-Narasimha; the capitals of 1137.

The storytelling rule: inside scenes events happen in order and with confidence; no scholar is named in scene prose; the Sala and Ramanuja stories and the finger tradition are told as ಐತಿಹ್ಯ and never shown as events. Choices disclosed in each scene's dramatised list: the sculptors' workshop; Bitti picking up the pendant at night; the full pot held literally and the year 1108; the envoy and the face-to-face reply; Derrett's battle shape with the boon before the victory (the records place it after); Adiyama and Dama as two men, Dama and Damodara as one; Kannegal mounted, after Talakad, no year; 'former Raya' read as Chavundaraya (1923) against the last Ganga king (Rice); the Kalyana homage placed near Sastri's 1122; the temple unfinished and Shantala present at the 1117 rite; an official reading her grant and her smile; the visit to her father, no cause, no sallekhana, 'not past forty'; the tent, the cradle, 'twenty-five years', the death year withheld in prose (1141 Rice, 1142 Derrett, c. 1152 Sastri), and the body carried to the capital (Derrett) rather than Sosavur (Rice).

Kannada: adult told-story register; no em dash; NFC; years only where dated or disclosed (1108 and 1116 are flagged in their dramatised lists, the subtitle carries ಸು.). story.facts is identical to facts.json (38 facts); every scene and didYouKnow id resolves and every fact is used. The summary states only what the scenes tell. The Hoysala dynasty entry in collections.json agrees with research section 1 (Nripa-Kama 1022–27, Vinayaditya, Ballala I 1100–1106, Vishnuvardhana c. 1108–1142 with the dispute, Narasimha I born 1133, Ballala II 22 July 1173, Narasimha II 1220–c. 1235, Someshvara's death marked disputed, Ballala III to 8 September 1342, last record 1346).
illustrations: All thirteen WebPs (cover, scene-01 to scene-12, 1600x900) were opened and compared with scene text, alt and bible/style.md, with enlarged crops of swords, headgear, banners, forts and inscribed surfaces. Three were regenerated after the first pass: the cover (helmeted soldiers and a crenellated castle among sand dunes), scene-04 (helmets, dunes, a sabre-like blade, a wrong Hoysala banner) and scene-09 (a gopura-like entrance tower). The replacements show a rubble fort in a river bend among palms and paddy, straight broadswords, white-turbaned spearmen, Sala-and-tiger banners on the Hoysala side and tiger banners in the Chola camp on the near bank, and a low carved soapstone porch with Sala groups and a scaffolded vimana, no gopura.

The king is the same man throughout: round face, short cropped beard, full moustache, tall tiered gold crown (cover, 03, 04, 05, 06, 09; greyer in 12); handsome and strong. In scene-02 the prince has only a moustache and his elder brother a beard. Gangaraja is consistent in this book: slim, long face, pointed beard, conical gold-banded cap, quilted coat (cover, 03, 04, 07, 08); in the Chavundaraya book's scene-11 he wears a jeweled fillet, so the disclosure claims only the face and pointed beard.

The Chalukya boar banner appears only on the Chalukya side (scene-07). The Chola tiger banner (scene-04, and one fallen in the river in scene-05) is historically right and disclosed. Shantala is dressed (scenes 09, 10). Digambara monks are seated in side view (scenes 08, 10); the colossus is shown legs-only. No gore. The coin in scene-06 is too small to carry letters; the slab in scene-10 has pseudo-strokes, not modern Kannada.

Nits recorded and not regenerated: scene-01's carved Sala looks feminine; scene-05's mounted officer (taken for Gangaraja) has a fuller beard, a brown helmet-like cap and a grid-patterned coat and is off-model; scene-07's following riders wear boots and seem to use stirrups; scene-08 has a small towered temple far off; scene-10 shows a later-looking pond with a pavilion in the plain; scene-12's women wear modern saree-and-blouse dress.
limitations: This is an AI review by a Claude agent; no human historian or epigraphist has read the text or checked the images.

Fact checking was limited to research/hoysala.md and research/hoysala-verified.md (EC II 1889 and 1923, EC V 1902, EC III 1894, Rice 1909, Derrett 1957 and Sastri 1958 as read for that file); primary sources were not re-fetched. MAR 1944 no. 34 (the 1098 'Vishnuvardhana'), the Ramanuja hagiographies, Kannegal's modern location, the six Narayana temples and any Talakadu-gonda coin photograph remain unverified, as the research file says.

No portrait of Vishnuvardhana, Shantala or Gangaraja survives; the Belur reliefs traditionally named for the king and queen are too small to give faces. All faces, the workshop, the camps, the mint, the tent and the twelfth-century buildings are reconstructions, as the disclosure says.
The Talakad battlefield geography (Hoysalas on the south bank, the fort across the river) follows the story's reading of Cn 209 and Derrett and is not established by any record.
Images were judged at 1600x900 WebP with enlarged crops; small distant details could not all be verified individually, and the nits above remain.
